chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hilal al-Razi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man appointed a man as his representative to divorce his wife when she menstruates and becomes pure. The man went out, and then it occurred to him (to change his mind), so he testified that he had annulled what he had ordered him to do, and that it had occurred to him regarding that. He (peace be upon him) said: So let him inform his wife, and let him inform the representative.

key_terms.فَبَدَا لَهُ: it occurred to him / he changed his mind

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for revoking a conditional divorce appointment if the husband changes his mind?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the revocability of conditional divorce agency, emphasizing that the principal retains the right to rescind the mandate before its execution. The requirement to notify both the wife and the agent underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ensuring clarity and preventing dispute in family law matters. It highlights the flexibility within the concept of *wakalah* (agency) in marital contracts, allowing the husband to alter his intent prior to the agent's finalization of the act.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hilal Al Razy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man appointed a man with the divorce of his wife when she menstruation and was pure, and the man went out. So he (later on) changed his mind, and kept witnesses that he has invalidated that matter, and that he had changed his mind with regards to that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him inform his wife, and let him inform the representative’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Muskan from abu Hilal al-Raziy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who appoints a man to divorce his wife after she experiences Hayd (menses) and becomes clean and he himself goes away; but he changes his mind and arranges witnesses that he has changed his mind. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must inform his wife and his attorney about it.’”
